title: Log env vars used during install
description: When installing, log which env vars were found and used in config resolution. This gives the user visibility into which env values influenced the install, complementing the source display already added to interactive prompts. Should work in both interactive and non-interactive modes, and show in --show and --check output.

title: Refactor config resolution to self-describing SourcedConfig pipeline
description:
Refactored the config resolution pipeline from named source fields (args/current/env/precedence) to a self-describing SourcedConfig type where each read function returns its source identity.

Changes:
- ConfigReadResult renamed to SourcedConfig with a source: ConfigFieldSource field
- resolveDesiredConfig now accepts sources: ReadonlyArray<SourcedConfig<TConfig>> instead of named args/current/env/precedence fields
- Array order IS precedence — no separate precedence field needed
- resolveDesiredConfig is now a pure combinator with no hidden readDefaultConfig call
- readCurrentPluginConfig accepts JsonObject | null instead of OpenCodePluginEntry, decoupling config reading from entry bookkeeping
- install-plan.ts builds the sources array with a local DEFAULT_PRECEDENCE and maps options.precedence when provided
- Removed sourceReadResult and DEFAULT_PRECEDENCE constant from config-sources.ts

This unblocks runtime use (gop-auto-discover-schema-runtime) because the same readCurrentPluginConfig function now works for both install-time (pass entry.options) and runtime (pass the options dict from opencode) without depending on OpenCodePluginEntry.

title: Install option to bake current env var values into config
description: Add an install-time option that resolves env vars to their current values and writes those literals into the opencode config file. This is the current default behavior — make it an explicit opt-in mode so users can intentionally choose to snapshot env values.
notes: Note: the 'bake' mode is more accurately 'skip env vars from install-time resolution'. The default install behavior should exclude env from the precedence chain so that only user-chosen values (args, existing config) and defaults are written. Env vars are resolved at runtime by the plugin, not baked into the config file. The bake/snapshot mode would be a separate explicit flag for users who want to pin current env values.

title: Install option to write {env:__} references into config
description: Add an install-time option that writes {env:VAR_NAME} token references into the opencode config file instead of resolved values. This delegates env var resolution to opencode's built-in {env:...} substitution at load time. Only applies to string fields where the schema defines an env mapping. The exact CLI flag/syntax is TBD.

title: Auto-load config schema at runtime via gop-config-discovery
description: When an opencode plugin starts up, it should be able to auto-load its ConfigSchema (via the gop-config-discovery mechanism from package.json exports) and use it for runtime config resolution. This would let a plugin call a single function like resolveRuntimeConfig(options) without manually wiring up schema discovery.

title: Show config sources in interactive prompts
description: When prompting for config values interactively, show the user where each value comes from. Currently promptMessage only shows (current: X, default: Y). It should also show env var names and values when present, so the user understands the full resolution picture. promptInitialValue should prefer env-resolved values over schema defaults explicitly. The observation data is already available in plan.resolvedConfig.fields[fieldName].observations.

title: Refine CLI arg-derived option boundaries
description: Track the args-tokens refactor direction from .test-agent/args.md. The goal is to use arg schema derived values for command-facing state while avoiding unnecessary domain option abstractions when they only duplicate CLI args.
design: Extract reusable CLI arg groups from installer command code. Prefer arg-derived values for thin command-facing utilities. Keep programmatic planning/runtime APIs domain-shaped when they represent durable concepts beyond CLI flags.
acceptance_criteria:
- Shared config args are extracted from installer command code.
- Config path resolution uses the chosen arg-derived boundary or a documented adapter shape.
- Install-specific command switches are separable from composed command args.
- Tests and type checks pass for the implemented slice.

title: Discover plugin config catalog by convention
description:
Add convention-over-configuration support so installer entrypoints can locate a plugin package's shared config catalog from a standard place instead of requiring every installer to manually import and pass it.

The current design expects callers to pass a descriptor with an explicit config schema/catalog. That is correct for a low-level API, but plugin packages would be easier to scaffold and maintain if this library also recognized a conventional config export path.

Candidate conventions to evaluate:

- package export subpath such as `./config` exposing the runtime-neutral catalog
- source path such as `src/config/catalog.ts` during TypeScript-first development
- descriptor metadata in package.json only for plugin id/default ref, while config remains code

This should preserve explicit descriptor/config passing as the reliable low-level escape hatch.
design:
Keep this as an additive feature after runtime/installer export boundaries are settled.

Likely shape:

- Define a small discovery API that returns either a resolved catalog/descriptor fragment or an explainable not-found result.
- Prefer package exports over raw source paths when resolving from installed packages.
- Allow TypeScript source paths in local development because Bun and modern Node workflows in this project run TS directly.
- Do not make runtime plugin code import installer modules while discovering config.
- Avoid dynamic magic in the core planner; discovery should happen in the installer shell or a separate convention module before calling the normal explicit APIs.
acceptance_criteria:
- A documented conventional config export path exists for OpenCode plugin packages.
- Installer code can use the convention with minimal boilerplate while still supporting explicit descriptor/config arguments.
- Runtime-safe imports remain free of Gunshi and prompt dependencies.
- Discovery failures produce actionable errors explaining which convention paths were checked.
- Tests cover package-export discovery, local TypeScript source discovery if supported, and fallback to explicit descriptor config.

title: Add --repair flag for invalid or unsupported config files
description:
Add a `--repair` flag for config files that cannot be safely edited as OpenCode config.

Repair means: back up the existing file, then overwrite it with a fresh valid `opencode.json` containing the target plugin entry. It is an explicit escape hatch for broken config files, not a general cleanup mode.

Repair v1 should cover:
- `invalid-json`: file exists but cannot be parsed as JSON, such as `{ plugin: [`.
- `unsupported-shape`: JSON parses, but the top-level value is not an object, such as `[]`, `"hello"`, `42`, `true`, or parsed `null`.

Default behavior without `--repair` should be conservative:
- `show` and `check` report `invalid-json` or `unsupported-shape` without throwing when possible.
- `install` refuses to write and gives a clear error explaining that repair is required.

`--repair` behavior:
- Implies `--backup`.
- Uses the existing backup path and `--backup-format` machinery.
- For `invalid-json` and `unsupported-shape`, plans a `create-config` replacement.
- Backs up the raw existing file text before overwriting.
- `--repair --dry-run` reports the repair plan, backup path, and replacement text without writing.

Non-goals for repair v1:
- Do not deduplicate duplicate plugin entries.
- Do not remove invalid plugin array entries.
- Do not sanitize invalid field values inside an otherwise readable target plugin tuple.
- Do not resolve ref conflicts; those remain normal unsafe actions handled by `--force` or later prompts.

Implementation implication: `invalid-json` currently exists in the type model but parse errors throw in the file-backed layer. Repair requires catching parse failures, representing `configState: "invalid-json"`, and preserving raw `previousText` so it can be backed up before replacement.
design:
Use the existing plan/apply split.

Planning:
- File-backed planning should catch JSON parse errors and pass an explicit invalid-json state into planning instead of throwing.
- Unsupported top-level values, including parsed `null`, should be distinguishable from a missing file.
- Without `--repair`, invalid or unsupported config states should produce a non-writing refusal plan/result that `show` and `check` can render.
- With `--repair`, invalid or unsupported config states should produce `action: "create-config"` with `safeNonInteractive` false unless repair is explicitly requested.

Filesystem/write behavior:
- `--repair` implies backup, so existing raw text must be written to the backup path before replacement.
- Missing files are not repair cases and do not need backup.
- Dry-run should compute but not create the backup.

CLI:
- Add `repair` to the relevant install args, ideally in a repair-owned arg group if/when repair grows enough to justify it.
- `--repair` should be accepted on install; show/check may expose repair-needed state but should not need the flag.
acceptance_criteria:
- `--repair` flag accepted by install command.
- `--repair` implies backup and respects `--backup-format`.
- Invalid JSON config without `--repair` is reported by `show`/`check` and refused by `install` with a clear error.
- Invalid JSON config with `--repair` produces `create-config`, backs up the raw broken text, and writes fresh config.
- Unsupported-shape config without `--repair` is reported by `show`/`check` and refused by `install` with a clear error.
- Unsupported-shape config with `--repair` produces `create-config`, backs up the raw existing text, and writes fresh config.
- Parsed JSON `null` is treated as unsupported-shape, not as a missing file.
- Missing config still uses the normal create-config path and does not require repair.
- `--repair --dry-run --json` reports repair action, backup path, `previousText`, `nextText`, and `written: false` without creating files.
- Repair does not dedupe plugin entries, remove invalid plugin array entries, sanitize invalid field values, or resolve ref conflicts.

title: Add --backup-format flag for backup filename pattern
description:
Add a `--backup-format` flag that controls the backup filename pattern used by `--backup`.

The format string supports placeholders:
- `{path}` — the full original config path (default pattern uses this as base)
- `{ext}` — the file extension (e.g. `.json`)
- `{name}` — the filename without extension
- `{dir}` — the directory containing the config file

Default format: `{path}.bak` (produces `opencode.json.bak`).

Examples:
- `--backup-format "{path}.bak"` → `opencode.json.bak` (default)
- `--backup-format "{dir}/{name}.backup{ext}"` → `opencode.backup.json`
- `--backup-format "{path}.{timestamp}"` → `opencode.json.2026-05-10T19:30:00Z`

`--backup-format` is ignored when `--backup` is not set.
acceptance_criteria:
- `--backup-format <pattern>` flag accepted by install command.
- Default pattern is `{path}.bak`.
- Pattern placeholders are substituted correctly.
- Invalid patterns produce a clear error.
- Ignored when `--backup` is not set.
close_reason: Implemented --backup-format with path/date placeholder interpolation and tests.

title: Add --backup flag to save config before writes
description:
Add a `--backup` flag that copies the current config file to a backup path before any write operation.

Behavior:
- When `--backup` is set and the install plan will write, copy the current file to a backup path before writing.
- Default backup path: `<config-path>.bak` (e.g. `opencode.json.bak`).
- If the config file doesn't exist yet (create-config), no backup is needed — skip silently.
- Backup happens before the write in `installOpenCodePluginToFile`.
- Should work with `--dry-run`: show that a backup would be created, but don't actually create it.

This is a prerequisite for `--repair` (`gop-repair`).
acceptance_criteria:
- `--backup` flag accepted by install command.
- Before writing, current config file is copied to backup path.
- No backup created when config file doesn't exist.
- `--dry-run` reports backup intent without creating the file.
- Human and JSON output include backup path when applicable.
close_reason: Implemented --backup and --backup-overwrite support with datestamped backup paths, JSON/human output fields, and tests.
